name: Uranus from Voyager 2, February 1, 1986
blurb: A planet that spins tipped on its side, about 51,100 kilometers across at the equator. Seen by Voyager 2's narrow-angle camera through orange, green, blue and violet filters: visible light only, 0.40 to 0.62 µm.
story: The whole of Uranus, as a crescent, from about 10 million kilometers away, 8 days after Voyager 2's closest approach to Uranus on January 24, 1986. Voyager 2's visit in January 1986 is still the only one any spacecraft has made to Uranus.

claims.text: about 51,100 kilometers across at the equator (JPL: equatorial radius 25559 km)
rotates at a nearly 90-degree angle from the plane of its orbit
Jan. 24, 1986: Voyager 2 made the first and so far only visit to Uranus
Voyager 2 closest approach to Uranus: January 24, 1986 17:59 UTC
10 million kilometers from Uranus's center when the green frame was taken (OPUS center distance 10,381,946 km)
phase angle 145 degrees (OPUS center phase angle)
